introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Further Mathematics Paper 3 (0775), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2021. Duration: two and a half hours.**

Answer ALL questions. For your guidance, the approximate mark allocation for parts of each question is indicated in brackets. Mathematical formulae and tables, published by the Board, and noiseless non-programmable electronic calculators are allowed. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage.

Question 8 (b) : la valeur critique est prise dans les tables de la loi normale, z = 1,96 (P(Z > 1,96) = 0,025), donc k = 16 + 3 x 1,96 = 21,88 ; la valeur exacte du quantile est 1,95996..., soit k = 21,88 à deux décimales.

questions.enonce_markdown:
A discrete random variable $X$ has probability mass function defined by

$$f(x) = \begin{cases} c\,(8 - x^2), & x = 1, 2 \\ c\,(17 - x^2), & x = 3, 4 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise.} \end{cases}$$

Find the value of the constant $c$. *[2 marks]*

A discrete random variable $X$ has probability mass function defined by

$$f(x) = \begin{cases} c\,(8 - x^2), & x = 1, 2 \\ c\,(17 - x^2), & x = 3, 4 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise.} \end{cases}$$

Find the median of $X$. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
With $c = \dfrac1{20}$, the cumulative probabilities are

$$P(X \le 1) = \frac{7}{20} = 0.35 < 0.5,\qquad P(X \le 2) = \frac{7 + 4}{20} = \frac{11}{20} = 0.55 \ge 0.5.$$

The cumulative probability first reaches $0.5$ at $x = 2$, so the median is $2$.

$$\boxed{\text{median} = 2}$$

questions.enonce_markdown:
A discrete random variable $X$ has probability mass function defined by

$$f(x) = \begin{cases} c\,(8 - x^2), & x = 1, 2 \\ c\,(17 - x^2), & x = 3, 4 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise.} \end{cases}$$

Find the mean and standard deviation of $X$. *[5 marks]*
A continuous random variable $Y$ has normal distribution with mean $16$ and variance $9$. Given that $P(Y > k) = 0.025$, determine the value of $k$. *[5 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
$Y \sim N(16, 9)$, so the standard deviation is $\sigma = 3$. Standardise with $Z = \dfrac{Y - 16}{3} \sim N(0, 1)$:

$$P(Y > k) = P\left(Z > \frac{k - 16}{3}\right) = 0.025.$$

Then $P\left(Z \le \dfrac{k - 16}{3}\right) = 1 - 0.025 = 0.975$. From the normal distribution tables, $\Phi(1.96) = 0.975$, so

$$\frac{k - 16}{3} = 1.96 \;\Longrightarrow\; k = 16 + 3\times 1.96 = 21.88.$$

$$\boxed{k = 21.88}$$
